title: Letter 37 — Put Down the Swings
attribution_note: Letter 37 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: I have heard that you have again restored the swings in Voronezh which had been put down. Do you not observe how much scandal and disorder is wrought at those swings by foolish and fearless men? Take heed, lest to you, as the giver of occasion for those disorders, all those scandals and lawless deeds which are done at those swings be reckoned by the judgment of God.

Perhaps you take care, for the sake of your own profit, to serve the fancies of men, which the Word of God commands us to root out? It is a lawless thing to seek one's profit in that which is the cause of the transgression of the law of God, and of dishonour to the Lawgiver, and of the ruin of men.

sections.heading: A time for repentance, not for amusement

pairs.en: The present time especially does not call for amusement, but for repentance, tears and weeping. Extremely senseless — and not only asleep, but dead in soul — is he who does not feel upon our Fatherland the hand of God for our sins. How many thousands of our brethren has the Prussian war swallowed up! How many widows and orphans has it left weeping, and how it has exhausted the common treasury! Everywhere fires multiply, failures of the harvest of grain, and the rest. We have not yet finished mourning that evil, and behold another, more fierce! Behold, again from the weapons of foreigners our Fatherland sighs and groans: again all is in confusion and fear, again our brethren receive wounds, again Christian blood is shed, again thousands of men fall lifeless, again the inconsolable weeping of fathers, mothers, wives and children has begun.

But what the end of this public evil will be is unknown; I know that without the help of God there is nothing from which to look for good. For it is not weapons that will save us, but the almighty help of God. But God has mercy and saves those who repent, and defends those who trust in Him, and not in silver and other things, and call upon Him with true zeal. How then, and where, shall there be repentance, where disorders and lawless deeds are not diminished, but multiplied?

sections.heading: Is it well for us to make merry?

pairs.en: And is it well for us in the Fatherland to make merry and fulfill our fancies, when our brethren beyond the borders always abide in every fear and sorrow? Is it for us to laugh and behave disorderly, when they give their heads under the sword, the bullets and the other weapons of the enemy for our sake — some receive wounds, some shed their blood, some are given over as a sacrifice to death? It is most unseemly and shameless!

Know, friend, that when they fall and are diminished, the matter comes home to us also. Therefore all must help the common calamity in common; and we shall help when our brethren defend us with weapons, and we by repentance and earnest tears and prayer assist their weapons. For so our merciful Lord will turn away His righteous wrath and defend us, will teach *the hands* of our brethren *to war, and their fingers to fight* [Psalm 143:1], *and will cover their heads in the day of battle* [Psalm 139:8].

But have you nothing whereby to feed yourself, save the swings? I think that even apart from them you have income. But if you would gather more and more, then take heed lest that terrible word of God touch you also, which was spoken to a certain rich man (it is written in the holy evangelist Luke, in the twelfth chapter, the twentieth verse). Read that parable and consider it.

If you hearken and put down the swings, you will do better both for your own soul and for others; but if you will not hearken, do as you will. Our faith teaches us that the Judgment of Christ will be, at which we shall all be gathered, and the apostle Paul has written by the Spirit of God that *“we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.* *And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.* *But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition”* [1 Timothy 6:7–9].
Be saved in Christ, brother and friend.
Your sincere well-wisher, the unworthy former bishop of Voronezh, Tikhon.
June 20, 1769. The Zadonsk Monastery.

I have written this, desiring the profit both of you and of the community. If I have heard falsely that you made the swings, then this does not concern you, and forgive me — perhaps we receive a false report also; but if it be true, then consider what has been written.
